column3: The Hebrew says “the whole commandment” and does not explicitly include “to give” after the LORD’s oath; BSB says “every commandment” and supplies “to give.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew explicitly says God caused the hunger, repeats “man” at the end, and says “everything proceeding from the LORD’s mouth” without a noun “word.” BSB says “in your hunger,” names man once, and supplies “word.”
The Hebrew has singular “your foot”; BSB has plural “your feet.”
The Hebrew says to know “with your heart”; BSB says “in your heart.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names “deeps” and uses singular “the valley” and “the mountain”; BSB has “springs” and plural “valleys and hills.”

The Hebrew says “bread” and actively states that you will hew copper from the mountains; BSB says “food” and describes the hills as “ready to be mined.”
